devdoc.details: The deployed code is `InlineRouterDispatch`'s runtime code followed by the routes, so it  is longer than this contract's compiled runtime code: a verifier must match it by its  creation code. Sourcify (and Blockscout, which uses it) does; Etherscan, which matches the  runtime code, cannot. Use `Router` where Etherscan verification matters.
devdoc.title: A router with its routes in its own code: the cheapest dispatch, verified by Sourcify

userdoc.notice: Create an immutable route and delegate function calls to their respective  implementations, up to 256 implementations and as many selectors as a deployment can carry:  about 4,800 under EIP-170's 24,576 bytes of code, and, on a chain with EIP-3860 (Shanghai  and later), about 1,460, since the constructor takes the routes ABI-encoded (32 bytes a  selector) and init code is at most 49,152 bytes there. A lookup reads the router's own code  (CODECOPY): no storage read and no other account touched, the cheapest of the routers here.
